correctness.rationale: Xie Theorem 1.2 gives lct I_(3,4)=11/2 and (5.1) gives dim J_L≤floor(13L/2). In the split quadratic space, choose a unit-parameter isotropic vector A and orthogonal transverse z with B(z,z)=1. Set v_1=A and v_j=A Y_j+t^a z W_j, a=floor(L/2). For even L, no W-constraints; for odd L impose W_3(0)=W_4(0)=0, W_2(0)≠0, making each pairwise residual product vanish modulo t^L. Count 5L+3a (even) or 5L+3(a+1)-2 (odd), giving floor(13L/2). The dual pairings with b,z recover Y and the truncated W coefficients, proving no fiber-dimension collapse. The L=1 case correctly gives dimension 6. Independently checked the parameter counts and first nonzero coefficient products for L=1..18.
